title: Latency-slope kernel estimator and tenant-aware phase slicer for prefill/decode
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Prefill/decode arbitration currently uses coarse phase splitting heuristics that don’t account for per-tenant latency sensitivity or kernel execution cost variance introduced by attention sparsity and quantized kernels. This results in suboptimal fairness (high-cost requests hogging slots) and missed latency SLOs for latency-sensitive tenants when throughput pressure rises.

Proposal: Implement a two-part runtime policy: (1) a lightweight latency-slope kernel estimator that predicts expected GPU kernel runtime for a request given (model variant, sequence length, attention-sparsity hint, quantization profile, and token phase), producing a scalar "kernel-cost-score"; (2) a tenant-aware phase slicer that uses kernel-cost-score and per-tenant latency-slope profiles to split prefill/decode work into micro-phases so that latency-sensitive tenants are granted prioritized micro-slices while throughput-oriented tenants accept larger consolidated slices. The slicer includes an optional hedging path to fall back to lower-cost model variants when predicted cost exceeds available headroom.

Goals: Reduce 95th latency for latency-tiered tenants by 15% under mixed workloads, maintain >=95% utilization for Dedicated pools, and avoid lowering overall throughput by more than 7% on median workloads.

Out of scope: full retraining of cost predictors, changes to kernel implementations themselves (this is orchestration layer only).
acceptance_criteria: Estimator runs at <200us median overhead per request on the control plane path
End-to-end 95th percentile latency for latency-tier requests improved by >=15% under the defined mixed workload benchmark
Overall token throughput decreases by <=7% on median batch of benchmarks compared to baseline
Feature flag gated rollout with metric safety checks and automatic revert on regression
Unit/integration tests for estimator logic and slice allocator added to runtime test harness
tasks: Design: define kernel-cost-score features and target distributions (Sofia)
Prototype: implement estimator shim in runtime routing (Ethan)
Integration: connect estimator output to phase slicer and quota arbiter (Ethan, Runtime)
Bench: create mixed-tenant workload harness with latency-tiered clients (Performance team)
Canary: rollout behind feature flag to 10% of Dedicated pools, track per-tenant P95 and throughput (SRE)
Docs: update console rollout docs and per-route config options (PM/Docs)
Monitoring: add kernel_cost_score histograms and slice allocation traces to tracing dashboard
notes: Estimator inputs: model_id, variant (float/quantized), sequence_lengths (prefill/decode), attention_density_hint (0-1), requested_priority, route_tags, and recent kernel_latency_stats for that model on the target GPU family.

We will implement a small online estimator using a linear model + lookup table for historical kernel latency by (model, variant, gpu_family, seq_len_bucket). Avoid heavy ML models to keep overhead tiny.
Tenant profile: maintain a compact per-tenant latency_slope parameter indicating willingness to trade throughput for lower latency; surfaced from Console (route config) and defaulted by plan tier.

Hedging policy: when kernel_cost_score > headroom_threshold, the allocator can either (A) split into more micro-slices and increase hedged early decode for latency requests, or (B) opportunistically route to compatible lower-cost variant (e.g., lower quantization, trimmed context) with user-configured permissiveness.
Tradeoffs: tighter prioritization reduces tail for latency tenants but can fragment batches, harming throughput. The goal is predictable bounded tradeoff and visibility in Console.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize estimator feature set and histogram buckets; add telemetry hooks
Week 2: implement estimator shim and basic LUT in runtime routing; unit tests
Week 3: implement phase slicer logic and integrate with quota arbiter; smoke tests
Week 4: run controlled benchmarks, tune headroom and slice sizes
Week 5: canary rollout + monitor, iterate on hedging thresholds
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: estimator mispredictions cause unfair starvation. Mitigation: conservative lower-bound estimates, emergency share guarantees, and circuit-breaker revert.
Risk: fragmentation harms throughput. Mitigation: limit maximum slices per request and use opportunistic consolidation for throughput-labeled tenants.
Risk: cross-tenant data exposure in profiling. Mitigation: only aggregate and store anonymized kernel latency statistics per model/gpu family; no customer payload retained
